speaker: Doctor
text: Please describe exactly where you feel the weakness and decreased sensation in your right arm, and when these symptoms first started?

speaker: Patient
text: 55-year-old male bodybuilder. The patient has been experiencing weakness in his right arm for a few weeks, which has progressively worsened to the point of dropping objects. He also reports a recent unexplained weight loss of 17 pounds and has a history of diabetes. The patient admits to chronic alcohol use, heavy smoking, and anabolic steroid use.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Given your significant weight loss, alcohol use, and steroid history, is the weakness localized specifically to the deltoid or biceps region, or does it involve the entire arm and shoulder? Also, do you have any numbness in the 4th and 5th fingers?

REQUEST TEST: CBC, Comprehensive Metabolic Panel, Liver Function Tests, TSH.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Weakness in the right arm. I also have Decreased sensation in the right arm, Dull aching and burning pain in the right arm, Significant weight loss.

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Diabetes Social history: Drinks 2-7 alcoholic beverages per day. Has smoked 2 packs of cigarettes per day since he was 25. Uses anabolic steroids.

speaker: Patient
text: Denies recent fevers, changes in vision, difficulty speaking, or changes in balance. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Multiple sclerosis and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text: That is interesting; however, your history of heavy alcohol use, steroid use, and the specific distribution of symptoms we are discussing do not align with Multiple Sclerosis. To determine if this is actually a brachial plexopathy, Pancoast tumor, or a metabolic neuropathy like Diabetic Amyotrophy, I need to see your imaging and lab results. REQUEST TEST: CBC, CMP, LFTs, TSH. REQUEST IMAGES: Chest_X-Ray, EMG_Nerve_Conduction_S Study_of_Right_Arm.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: COMPLETE_BLOOD_COUNT: WBC Within normal limits, Hemoglobin Within normal limits, Platelets Within normal limits; COMPREHENSIVE_METABOLIC_PANEL: NORMAL READINGS; LIVER_FUNCTION_TESTS: NORMAL READINGS; TSH: NORMAL READINGS; CHEST_X-RAY: Findings Mass noted at the apex of the right lung; CT_CHEST: Findings Solid mass at the apex of the right lung, suggestive of a tumor

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Pancoast Tumor (Superior Sulcus Tumor) causing Brachial Plexopathy.

The chest imaging confirms a solid mass at the apex of the right lung, which perfectly explains your shoulder/arm weakness and sensory changes. Given your history of smoking and weight loss, this is highly suspicious for malignancy. We need to evaluate if the tumor has invaded surrounding structures like the ribs or brachial plexus. REQUEST IMAGES: MRI_Chest_with_Contrast.
